_doc: OPS-FORBIDDEN-PHRASE-ENUMERATION-AND-WEBHOOKS-DOC-W1 CH1 R1.1 — estate-sampled DIRTY fixtures.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/check-forbidden-phrases.mjs used to claim, in a comment, that its
DIRTY fixtures were 'the ACTUAL retired phrases from the estate census'. For retired-tier-quotas
that was FALSE: the fixture was authored FROM the regex ('Starter includes 3,000 calls and Pro
15,000 calls a month.') rather than sampled from live copy, so the pattern and its proof shared
one author and one blind spot. The pattern demanded the unit noun `calls` immediately after the
figure; the live estate rendered the ladder as a slash-delimited enumeration with the noun far to
the left, and the gate reported PASS over it for 30 days.
A fixture recorded here is bytes LIFTED from a live surface at a named SHA — never retyped, never
reconstructed from the pattern it is supposed to test. scripts/check-forbidden-phrases.mjs reads
this file in --self-test and asserts its own DIRTY fixture for each id EQUALS the sample recorded
here, so the provenance is VERIFIED rather than declared (CH3). A phrase with no estate sample
declares `synthetic_reason` in ops/forbidden-phrases.json instead; synthetic is permitted,
undeclared is not.
🛑 THE RETIRED BYTES BELOW ARE THE POINT. Do not 'fix' them to current copy — this file is a
record of what the gate MISSED, and correcting it would delete the only evidence the miss ever
happened. tests/** is deliberately outside the scan corpus of ops/forbidden-phrase-targets.json
(measured: 0 of 444 resolved rows), so these bytes cannot trip the gate they exist to prove.

retired-tier-quotas.sample: a pull call (Free 100 / Starter 3,000 / Pro 15,000 / Enterprise 100,000).
retired-tier-quotas.note: Sampled from live estate copy, NOT authored from the regex. This is the shape the pattern missed: the unit noun appears ONCE, far to the left ('a pull call'), so `\b3,000\s+calls` could never match it. Verified plain ASCII — no NBSP, thin space or zero-width character — by JSON round-trip of the raw line.

_doc: NOT keyed by a phrase id, and deliberately so: no pattern in ops/forbidden-phrases.json addresses
webhook lifecycle semantics, so this passage was invisible to the gate and would have stayed
invisible even if the quota pattern were widened. It is recorded as the second half of the CH1
defect and as the standing counter-example to 'the gate is green, therefore the doc is true'.
Underscore-prefixed so a per-id lookup can never mistake it for a phrase entry.

webhook-auto-disable-recreate.sample:
- **Auto-disable:** an endpoint that fails 20 deliveries in a row is paused
  automatically. Fix it (it must return `2xx`), then recreate the subscription.
webhook-auto-disable-recreate.note: FALSE since OPS-WEBHOOK-SUBSCRIBER-NOTIFY-W1. The lifecycle self-heals: consecutive failures move a subscription to `quarantined` (src/lib/webhooks-store.ts), a health probe resumes it on any 2xx (src/lib/webhook-delivery.ts, '[webhook-probe] sub N probe 2xx -> resumed active'), and the recovery window is tier-differentiated 30d paid / 7d free (src/lib/webhook-quarantine-policy.ts). A subscriber who followed this sentence would destroy and recreate a subscription that was about to recover on its own.
